new.brief: Creates a new `GtkFileFilter` with no rules added to it.
new.md:
Creates a new `GtkFileFilter` with no rules added to it.

Such a filter doesn’t accept any files, so is not
particularly useful until you add rules with
[`FileFilter.add_mime_type()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FileFilter#method:add_mime_type),
[`FileFilter.add_pattern()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FileFilter#method:add_pattern),
[`FileFilter.add_suffix()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FileFilter#method:add_suffix) or
[`FileFilter.add_pixbuf_formats()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FileFilter#method:add_pixbuf_formats).

To create a filter that accepts any file, use:
```c
GtkFileFilter *filter = gtk_file_filter_new ();
gtk_file_filter_add_pattern (filter, "*");
```

new_from_gvariant.brief: Deserialize a file filter from a `GVariant`.
new_from_gvariant.md:
Deserialize a file filter from a `GVariant`.

The variant must be in the format produced by
[`FileFilter.to_gvariant()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FileFilter#method:to_gvariant).

doc.brief: Filters files by name or mime type.
doc.md:
Filters files by name or mime type.

`GtkFileFilter` can be used to restrict the files being shown in a
file chooser. Files can be filtered based on their name (with
[`FileFilter.add_pattern()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FileFilter#method:add_pattern) or [`FileFilter.add_suffix()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FileFilter#method:add_suffix))
or on their mime type (with [`FileFilter.add_mime_type()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FileFilter#method:add_mime_type)).

Filtering by mime types handles aliasing and subclassing of mime
types; e.g. a filter for text/plain also matches a file with mime
type application/rtf, since application/rtf is a subclass of
text/plain. Note that `GtkFileFilter` allows wildcards for the
subtype of a mime type, so you can e.g. filter for image/\*.

Normally, file filters are used by adding them to a file chooser
(see [`FileDialog.set_filters()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FileDialog#method:set_filters)), but it is also possible to
manually use a file filter on any [`FilterListModel`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FilterListModel) containing
`GFileInfo` objects.

# GtkFileFilter as GtkBuildable

The `GtkFileFilter` implementation of the `GtkBuildable` interface
supports adding rules using the `<mime-types>` and `<patterns>` and
`<suffixes>` elements and listing the rules within. Specifying a
`<mime-type>` or `<pattern>` or `<suffix>` has the same effect as
as calling
[`FileFilter.add_mime_type()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FileFilter#method:add_mime_type) or
[`FileFilter.add_pattern()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FileFilter#method:add_pattern) or
[`FileFilter.add_suffix()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FileFilter#method:add_suffix).

An example of a UI definition fragment specifying `GtkFileFilter`
rules:
```xml
<object class="GtkFileFilter">
  <property name="name" translatable="yes">Text and Images</property>
  <mime-types>
    <mime-type>text/plain</mime-type>
    <mime-type>image/ *</mime-type>
  </mime-types>
  <patterns>
    <pattern>*.txt</pattern>
  </patterns>
  <suffixes>
    <suffix>png</suffix>
  </suffixes>
</object>
```

add_mime_type.brief: Adds a rule allowing a given mime type.
add_mime_type.md: Adds a rule allowing a given mime type.

add_mime_types.brief: Adds a rule allowing a given array of mime types.
add_mime_types.md:
Adds a rule allowing a given array of mime types.
It can for example be used with
[Gly.Loader.get_mime_types](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/glycin/libglycin/type_func.Loader.get_mime_types.html).

This is equivalent to calling [`FileFilter.add_mime_type()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FileFilter#method:add_mime_type)
for all the supported mime types.

add_pattern.brief: Adds a rule allowing a shell style glob pattern.
add_pattern.md:
Adds a rule allowing a shell style glob pattern.

Note that it depends on the platform whether pattern
matching ignores case or not. On Windows, it does, on
other platforms, it doesn't.

add_pixbuf_formats.brief: Adds a rule allowing image files in the formats supported by `GdkPixbuf`.
add_pixbuf_formats.deprecated_md:
Use the api of your image loading framework (e.g. glycin)
  to enumerate supported formats
add_pixbuf_formats.md:
Adds a rule allowing image files in the formats supported by `GdkPixbuf`.

This is equivalent to calling [`FileFilter.add_mime_type()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FileFilter#method:add_mime_type)
for all the supported mime types.

add_suffix.brief: Adds a suffix match rule to a filter.
add_suffix.md:
Adds a suffix match rule to a filter.

This is similar to adding a match for the pattern "*.`suffix`"

An exaple to filter files with the suffix ".sub":
```c
gtk_file_filter_add_suffix (filter, "sub");
```

Filters with multiple dots are allowed.

In contrast to pattern matches, suffix matches
are *always* case-insensitive.

get_attributes.brief: Gets the attributes that need to be filled in for the `GFileInfo` passed to this filter.
get_attributes.md:
Gets the attributes that need to be filled in for the `GFileInfo`
passed to this filter.

This function will not typically be used by applications;
it is intended for use in file chooser implementation.

get_name.brief: Gets the human-readable name for the filter.
get_name.md:
Gets the human-readable name for the filter.

See [`FileFilter.set_name()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.FileFilter#method:set_name).

set_name.brief: Sets a human-readable name of the filter.
set_name.md:
Sets a human-readable name of the filter.

This is the string that will be displayed in the user interface
if there is a selectable list of filters.

to_gvariant.brief: Serialize a file filter to an `a{sv}` variant.
to_gvariant.md: Serialize a file filter to an `a{sv}` variant.

mime-types.brief: The MIME types that this filter matches.
mime-types.md: The MIME types that this filter matches.

name.brief: The human-readable name of the filter.
name.md:
The human-readable name of the filter.

This is the string that will be displayed in the user interface
if there is a selectable list of filters.

patterns.brief: The patterns that this filter matches.
patterns.md: The patterns that this filter matches.

suffixes.brief: The suffixes that this filter matches.
suffixes.md: The suffixes that this filter matches.
